Being new in medical practice, this method allows one to determine subsurface distributions of dielectric permittivity and conductivity of a medium by using the results of measuring the impedance of small antennas which are located on the medium surface and included in resonant sensors. As a probing element, we use the edge capacity of a cylindrical condenser with external coating and a metal flange end. Such a configuration of the near-field antenna makes it possible to minimize the negative influence of the pressing and measurements data distortions caused by the pressure of the sensor on the biological tissue. We work out a theoretical approach to finding the dependences of impedance characteristics of the near-field antennas, which contact the surface of a medium characterized by an inhomogeneous profile of the complex permittivity, and present examples of solving the inverse problem for subsurface probing in the case of layered media.

articleTitle: Transition radiation of a relativistic point charge on the transverse orientation linear antenna
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The induced charge and current distribution along the transverse orientation linear antenna, while its surface is intersected by the relativistic point charge, has been calculated. The wave packet of the current with a step and delta-shaped fronts extends along the antenna. A normal component of the transition-radiation electric field is calculated. The normal component of the electric field, having a maximum along the normal to the antenna axis, is distributed in the form of a diverging spherical wave with a delta-shaped front. The uncompensated normal component of the transitionradiation electric field strength in the wave zone is a wave packet of different-polarity delta-shaped pulses. The delta-shaped pulses are related to the relativistic charge radiation itself and to the relativistic charge radiation reflected from the target. The relativistic charge radiation reflected from the target is much higher than the radiation of the relativistic charge itself.

Author Keywords: normal component of the electric field

articleTitle: Theoratical research of resonant characteristics of metal-dielectric difraction gratings
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Theoretical research of resonance properties of metal-dielectric gratings is presented. These gratings are two-dimensional periodic structures formed by the dielectric nanorods, which stand on the multilayer structure, which consists of metal and dielectric nano films. Theoretical results obtained are based on the rigorous solution of the integral differential volume equation by dint of the Galerkin's method for the diffraction of electromagnetic waves which incident on the 2-d periodic diffraction grating. The final value of the dielectric permeability of metals is considered. New diffraction grating obtained can absorb more than 90% of the solar energy of the radiation in a wide range of wavelengths and angles of incidence. It is shown that the use the wavelength of the resonance absorption depends on the type of material of the metal film and the use of two films of different metals results in a broadband absorption. The result obtained can be applied in the solar battery design.

articleTitle: Microwaves can reduce the effects of ionizing radiation on biological objects
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: If the intensity of microwave radiation of less than 10 mW·cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> the increase in radioresistance is realized. In the case where the intensity of the microwaves is greater than 10 mW·cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>, radio-resistance is reduced. It is shown that low intensity microwave provides an increase in the permeability of cell membranes, but the temperature of the cell, has not changed. This increases the enzymatic activity, thereby increasing to radioresistance of biological object. Powerful microwaves, on the contrary, much heated to the biological cells, contributing to their destructions. The presence of disruptive disorders in a cell lowers resistance bioobject to the ionization radiation.

articleTitle: Enhanced algorithms for communication or navigation adaptive antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The report discusses adaptation algorithms to minimize the three goal functions each of them reflects more or less adequately the requirements imposed on communication or navigation systems. The properties of adaptive antennas in settling states and their block diagrams are discussed. The special coefficient called the coefficient of adaptation efficiency is introduced to compare the different versions of adaptive antennas. It is the ratio of the areas (or volumes) of the working area after adaptation and without it. We present stochastic characteristics of the adaptation efficiency that was obtained in the simulation of a large number of random interferers' situations.

articleTitle: Microwave radiation of the column of isotropic and magnetized plasma
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In this paper the antenna of a traveling wave, which represents a column of isotropic plasma or the plasma column, placed in an external infinitely large magnetic field is studied both theoretically and numerically and compared between them. Plasma is assumed cold and collisionless. The dependence of radiation patterns upon plasma density, geometric parameters of plasma cylinder and radiation wavelength is investigated. At that it is considered not only linear, but also short-wave antenna radiating wavelengths close to the antenna radius. In an isotropic plasma column (B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> = 0) and in the magnetized (B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> = ∞), there are only a slow plasma E-wave with frequencies lower the plasma frequency. We study axially symmetric E-wave. Solutions of the dispersion equations give the dependence of the frequency on the wavevector, necessary to calculate the radiation patterns. The wave in plasma cylinder induces a wave of current density. Knowing the current it is possible to calculate the radiation field in the far field and, accordingly, the normalized radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Flat ring fractal antenna
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Considered flat ring fractal antennas by iterations of 1st and 2nd order. Analyses and comparison of frequency dependencies input impedance, module of reflection coefficient of considered antennas is organized on the base of computer simulation. The obtained results clearly show the advantages and disadvantages of the models under investigation.

articleTitle: Electrodynamics basics and duality principle
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The given report proposes general and consistent statement of the classical electrodynamics basis using axiomatic and duality principles for its construct. Vector algebra and vector analysis are created by the application of the duality principle. The last fact allows formulating Maxwell equations in strictly symmetric form. It means the statement of electrodynamics postulates (axioms) under a principle of duality. Electrodynamics basis construction begins immediately using its postulates formulated for electromagnetic field arbitrary excitation.

articleTitle: Researches of receiving-rectifying element of the rectennas for wireless power transmission systems to remote objects
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Potential abilities of receiving-rectifying elements (RRE) of rectennas based on Schottky diodes are estimated. In paper is suggested emitting structure of RRE which receive field on orthogonal polarizations, which allows increasing specific power of direct-current, collecting from square meter of rectenna aperture, decreasing its weight and dimensions and increasing its reliability.

articleTitle: Maximum likelihood esimation of broadband noise source location for unknown signal and noise power spectral densities
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Maximum likelihood estimator of broadband Gaussian noise source location in the presence of spatially uncorrelated background noise with adaptation to the unknown power spectral densities of noise and source signal is considered; the difference of the estimator from the analogous estimators derived earlier is discussed. The Cramer-Rao Lower Bound (CRLB) for characterization of location estimate variance is derived. The comparison of empirical variance estimates with CRLB and with empirical variance estimates in the case of conventional summation of narrow band array outputs is conducted. It is shown that the technique proposed provides better accuracy when the signal and noise power spectral densities are appreciable different. It is shown also that the effects of weak spatial noise correlation are negligible.

articleTitle: Features of a choice of a spherical reflector geometrical parameters
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: A method for determining the diameter of the aperture spherical reflector over the allowed phase errors and the relationship of the focal distance to diameter aperture is present.

articleTitle: Nature of extraordinary transmission through a metal screen slit filled with a metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The analytical solution of the scalar two-dimensional problem of TM-wave diffraction by a single subwavelength slit perforated in a thick perfectly conducting screen and filled with a metamaterial is obtained. The phenomenon of extraordinary transmission through the slit filled with the epsilon-negative or double-negative media is discovered. The dependence of the slit transmittance on the problem parameters is presented. The analysis of the slit electromagnetic response clearly reveals the unity of physical nature of the conventional Fabry-Perot resonances and the extraordinary transmission peak emerged in the evanescent-mode regime of the slit. It is shown that the negative plasma-like frequency-dependent dielectric acts as a qualitative model of the dispersive properties of the below-cutoff holes perforated in a screen. The results of the physical analysis of diffraction by the two-dimensional geometry under study are generalized to the case of three-dimensional hole structures.

articleTitle: Influence of antenna electromagnetic parameters on radio link transmission coefficient
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The numerical analysis of radio link transmission coefficient on the basis of the electromagnetic model which allowed to consider the partial mismatch of antennas with transmission link, the antenna polarization mismatch, their mutual coupling is presented. The results can be generalized for the case of multiantenna system at the radio link input and output in the analysis of MIMO-channel capacity.

articleTitle: Wave processes in near zone of Hertz dipole with plane screen
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The physical peculiarities of the wave processes in the whole space in a near-field zone of Hertz dipole placed over ideally conducting plane screen are analyzed. The amplitudes, phases and phase velocities of electric and magnetic fields (EMF) components in the direction of a normal to the screen versus the distance from a dipole to observation point R' are calculated. It is shown, that the velocity of decreasing the EMF amplitudes are smaller than in case of a dipole in a free space. Modulus of the transverse EMF components ratio equals the wave impedance in a free space beginning with R'≅λ. The ratio argument equals zero and the phase velocities of EMF components coincide with the ones in case of a dipole in a free space beginning with R'=0.52λ. The boundary of far-field zone depends also from the observation angles.

articleTitle: Microwave H-sectorial horn radiator with the return radiation reduced level
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: H-sectorial horn radiator of the electromagnetic waves of microwave range with the reduced level of the return radiation arising on the edge of its aperture outlet has been developed. Return radiation level reduction is realized by the method of antiphase excitation of the slowed down surface waves on the external side of the horn radiator rim aperture.

articleTitle: New manufacturing technology of microwave elements and units for communication and navigation systems
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: A new microwave integration technology of electroplating is proposed, which combines formation and mounting of multilayer structures. It uses a minimal amount of flanges in the waveguide communication lines for extrahigh frequency (EHF), and is capable also to integrate the metallic and non-metallic parts into the waveguide structure with no detachable elements. Products' weight and dimensions were significantly reduced while ensuring their sufficient rigidity and strength. The mechanical machining, gold and silver coatings were totally excluded; components' and units' parameters were improved. The settings and adjustment of the finished product were greatly simplified.

articleTitle: Antenna system for radiomonitoring
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The theoretical ratio, based on which can be built the structure of antenna system, are described.

Author Keywords: the intensity of the electromagnetic field

articleTitle: Upgrades to the Kharkiv V. N. Karazin National University MF radar antenna
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The Kharkiv V. N. Karazin National University MF radar has been widely employed to study mesospheric electrodynamics in the altitude range from 60 to 70 km where the electron density values remain below 100 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>. On the other hand, the technique developed at the University for investigating mesospheric electrodynamics demands signal-to-noise ratios greater than five. In addition, a major contribution to signal degradations makes radio interference, and consequently the radar has to operate in a frequency range at the upper end of the medium frequency band, and the antenna array cannot be designed to be resonant. The purpose of this paper is to report the upgrades to the MF radar antenna array to achieve maximum signal-to-noise ratio values. First, the replacement of a point resistive load by a resistor-capacitor load has provided the improvement in the impedance match of the existing antenna to the feeder. The voltage standing wave ratio in the 1.9-3 MHz frequency band could reach 3 before the replacement and does not exceed a value of 1.75 thereafter. Further, the upgrades put forward to the individual antenna arrangement resulted in converting three-lobe antenna pattern only into one-lobe symmetric antenna pattern and low levels of sidelobes over the entire 1.5-3.5 MHz frequency band.

articleTitle: Computational model of microcoplanar strip antennas
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: A various types of strip antennas for spin waves excitation are considered. The computation scheme for microcoplanar strip antenna is presented. The method of numerical solution of singular integral equation for current is proposed.

articleTitle: Antenna arrays: Waveguide layout designing automation
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Waveguide layout designing automation in the large-sized phased antenna arrays is studied. A new methodology of the automation and algorithms based on the flexible connection routing method are suggested. Results are realized in the software module WDS (Waveguide Design Solution) based on SolidWorks system. This module gives an opportunity to decrease design and engineering time and costs.

articleTitle: Optimization of geometric parameters of antenna with a logarithmic frequency
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The results of theoretical and experimental research of trapezoidal antenna with a logarithmic frequency are submitted in this article; its geometric parameters are chosen and frequency properties are defined.

articleTitle: The formation of zero levels of radiation pattern liner antennas array with minimum quality of controlling elements
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In this article we consider the one of the ways of forming the zero-lobe levels of a linear antenna array with a minimum quality of elements which controlled by the spatial filter processing.

articleTitle: The influence of the screen on the characteristics of omnidirectional radiators and rarefied arrays
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Hertz dipole radiation pattern and the in-phase half-wave dipole arrays of these radiators have been calculated for the case where the half-wave vibrator is over an infinite perfectly conducting screen at a height h, and the distance between the transmitters at random lattices and the amplitude distribution of the currents on the grill evenly. The calculations were performed in the whole space of observation. The algorithms and computer programs to calculate CPV investigated radiator s and arrays. It is shown that there is a distance between the radiator s in the sparse grid at which the maximum maximorum CPV (as in the case of gratings in free space). It is shown that when h = 0,25λ the optimal distance between the transmitters than 1.15 wavelength (grating in free space d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">opt</sub> ≈ 0,9 λ).

articleTitle: Analysis of the technical state of cable lines of local connection
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The short analysis of the technical state of cable lines of single-site networks of connection is made, local town telephone networks and rural telephone networks which are built on the cables T and KCΠΠ types accordingly.

articleTitle: Radiation patterns of antennas beyond line-of-sight and errors of transmitter position finding in multistatic systems
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Distortions of instant radiation patterns of transmitting antennas on different heights of source over Earth's surface are considered. It is shown that accuracy of source position finding after secondary processing may be sufficient for using triangulation in many cases in the multistatic systems.

articleTitle: Application of antenna theory with nonlinear elements for MIMO analysis
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: It is shown that when an electrodynamic network model is used for a MIMO system, such a system can be represented as an antenna with nonlinear elements (ANE) consisting of linear and nonlinear multipole networks. The multipoles are described using component equations and are connected using systems of state and output equations. Furthermore, all nonlinear elements of the system (due to the presence of nonlinear devices in transceiving circuits, control and switching elements in radiating systems, nonlinear loads, scatterers, etc.) are included in a separate nonlinear network, which allows for physical-layer MIMO system analysis and optimization time reduction, taking into account various nonlinear devices and reconfigurable elements.

articleTitle: Electrodynamic analysis of optical nanoplasmonic structures
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In the paper the rigorous solution of vectorial integro-differential equation of diffraction on three dimensional dielectric bodies with complex permittivity was derived by means of Galerkin method. The solution was applied to investigate the diffraction of electromagnetic waves on doubly periodic metallic gratings, to investigate the properties of eigenwaves of nanowaveguides and photonic crystals. The possibility of creation of grating with low coefficients of reflection and transmission at plasmonic resonance was shown. The validity of application of method of approximate boundary conditions for thin dielectric layer considering finite value of metals' permittivity in optical frequency for calculation of structures, which contain nanoscale metallic layers, was proved.

articleTitle: Robust estimation of radiation sources in an array of electric dipoles
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Approach to robust estimation of radiation sources in an array of electric dipoles when measurement data are distorted by additive noise as well as by random impulses is suggested. It is based on a non-linear optimization technique where objective function is built by the idea of minimization of “spatial extent.” The model of radiation sources is described by a set of ideal Hertzian dipoles. The case, when dipoles are located along a straight line, which is parallel to measurement line of electric field, and when their electric moments are perpendicular to the measurement plane, is considered. Algorithm, based on conjugate gradient method, is proposed. Numerical simulations are presented.

articleTitle: Spectral properties of a broken-symmetry two-ridged rectangular waveguide section
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Influence of a symmetry breaking in a two-ridged rectangular waveguide section on its frequency response is numerically investigated. Section is formed by two rectangular inserts arranged near each other in a cross section of a rectangular waveguide. It is found that a symmetry breaking results in generation of additional attenuation pole at the section frequency response. A pole generation mechanism is studied within the concept of the spectral theory of open waveguide resonators. It is interpreted as a result of excitation of a number of natural oscillations of the complex frequencies. Possibilities to provide a filtering function with both a lower-frequency and a higher-frequency attenuation poles are shown.

articleTitle: Polarization mode dispersion compensator based on anizotropic properties of spiral-bended single-mode fibers
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Has been developed a polarization mode dispersion compensator for singlemode optical fiber using artificially created difference of phase velocities propagation of basic extraordinary and ordinary waves in spiral-bended optical fiber, coiled tight turn to turn on the dielectric core.

articleTitle: Measuring the performance of active phased array antennas on a compact antenna test range of collimator type “AKK1-12”
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In this work we report measurements of integral characteristics and energy performance of active phased array antennas over L and X bands. Measurements were performed using a compact antenna test range of collimator type “AKK1-12” located at JSC “NIIP” (V.V. Tikhomirov Research and Development Institute for Instrument Engineering).

articleTitle: The circuit design of excitation of the 144 element patch antenna array with operated polarization
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The block diagram of the distribution device is developed for a 144-element array of the patch irradiators, consisting of four subsystems, each of which provides excitation of two ports in the four-element clusters. Necessary switchings in the distribution device for maintenance of demanded regimes of excitation it is carried out at the expense of the commutator, thus phase shifters are excluded from the excitation circuit design.

articleTitle: L-band airborne linear aesa design features
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: L-band linear small element AESA for airborne radar is considered. Main problems and design features of linear airborne L-band AESA are shown. Key characteristics of AESA devices and typical radiation patterns of linear L-band AESA are presented. Results of L-band airborne AESA energetic efficiency estimation are shown. Design opportunity of two-dimensional AESA based on linear AESA devices is considered.

articleTitle: Linear array loop antenna with series excitation, with sector-shaped and isotropic directional pattern in electric plane
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Some results of numerical modeling of a linear array with series excitation are presented. Loop antennas with array perimeter length close to the wavelength are radiating elements. Sector-shaped pattern is formed when using a reflector, an isotropic (quasi-isotropic) by modification of the geometry of the array.

articleTitle: Research of electro-optical modulators usage for microwave photonic filters
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: We analyze the most effective way to obtain microwave-photonic filter's coefficients, specifically implemented by electro-optical modulators. These devices are attractive to obtain desired number and sign of coefficients which results in high tunability and reconfigurability of filters. One has to decide which device will be the most appropriate in obtaining desired frequency response of the filter.

articleTitle: Numerical analyses of planar waveguide PAA with external dielectrical sheets by penetrating area method
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Numerical analyses of planar waveguide phased array antennas with external dielectrical sheets by penetrating area method (PAM) is presented. The features of PAM's application for calculating 3D electrodynamics problem is discussed. Obtained results are demonstrated that application of the proposed method matches with well-known results and can be used for analyses and investigation 3D electrodynamics problems.

articleTitle: Theoretical investigation of plasmonic nanowaveguide structures and photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: A vector integral-differential equation to describe electromagnetic waves propagation in nanowaveguides and photonic crystals containing thin metal layers is developed. Exact solution of the equation is obtained with Galerkin method taking into account complex dielectric permittivity of metals in optical range. A simple method to find complex propagation constant for low-loss waveguide structures is developed and proved. Surface plasmon-polariton (SPP) waves were simulated in the structures under consideration.

articleTitle: Calculating antenna characteristics within the framework of waveguide representation of HF electromagnetic field
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: We consider the problem of effects of transmitting and receiving antennas' characteristics in the structural physical model of the HF radio channel. The radio channel consists of transmitting-receiving antenna-feeder paths and the Earth-ionosphere waveguide. Characteristics of the radio channel are calculated using the normal wave method. The solution is obtained within the framework of waveguide representation of the HF electromagnetic field in the spherical waveguide Earth-ionosphere. Wire antennas with arbitrary configuration are also considered.

Author Keywords: coefficients of excitation and reception of normal waves

articleTitle: Development of the theory of nanoantennas based on modulated plasmon-polariton structures
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: This work presents a review of development of the theory of plasmon - polariton structures and nanoantennas based on them. It shows the method for solving the problem of excitation of impedance structures, modulated by multiple periodic sequences of impulse functions by an external source of electromagnetic field. The algorithm and the recurrence formula are proposed for the construction of mathematical models of a wide class of elements of infocommunication systems based on structures with N-fold periodicity. A comparative analysis is provided of the influence of the form of impulse sequences on the formation of spatial distribution of radiation field. Parameters for the design of nanoantennas, spatial filters, interferometers, commutators, superlenses and supercollimators have been calculated.

articleTitle: The printed leaky-wave array
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: A leaky-wave antenna array is one of the attractive candidates for high efficiency and low cost planar antennas in centimeter- and millimeter-wave applications such as automotive radars and radio communication devices. In this paper, a planar leaky-wave antenna array composed of a printed periodic metal strip grating on a grounded dielectric waveguide and using a coplanar feeding device for the dielectric waveguide is proposed. Antenna design examples and their simulated radiation characteristics for 10, 4-10, 8 GHz, 24-24, 4 GHz and 36, 5-37, 3 GHz frequency ranges are presented.

articleTitle: Carbon nanotubes interference
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: At present much attention is given to the scattering properties of the composite materials containing the incorporation of carbon nanotubes due to the prospects for their application to different branches of science and technology. To study successfully the structure and properties of such materials with the radio spectroscopy method it is essential to know their electrodynamical properties. In this case such structures are characterized by a sufficient complexity of their geometry (CNT location and orientation), and, as a result, by a complexity of their electrodynamical properties. Interaction interference in the composite materials consisting of carbon nanotubes is considered in the report. Mutual resistance dependences on the carbon nanotubes distance and shift relative to each other in a wide frequency range are derived. The obtained results are discussed.

articleTitle: Some simplifications of acoustic antennas theory, due to the features of environment reaction
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The influence of air resistance on the motion of mechano-acoustic level of acoustic antenna is considered. Using basic equations of hydrodynamics and with the principle of similarity proposed simplified relations for the calculation of oscillatory processes in electro-acoustic transducers of acoustic antennas.

articleTitle: Horizontal electrical dipole radiation out of a dielectric ball shielded by a spherical segment
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The regularization tasks of the horizontal electrical dipole radiation out of a sphere with the circular aperture with dielectrical ball loading are constructed and analyzed. We discussed of the separation of the boundary conditions for scalar electrical and magnetical potentials Debaya on the ideal conductivity spherical segment and on the aperture. We use of the method of the separation variables in the spherical system coordinate. We solve auxiliary integral equations of Abel's type and select main parts of 4 functional equations by introducing two small parameters. As a result we obtain two disconnected linear algebraic systems of second kind with compact matrix operators of Fredholm's type. Some characteristics of the spherical antenna by improvement of analytical-computational method are discussed.

Author Keywords: sphere with circular aperture and inner ball

articleTitle: Recent advances in terahertz science at Queen Mary University of London
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: This paper aims to highlight recent activities in THz group at QMUL. These include progress in data processing techniques related to material parameter extraction procedures, characterization of water-based highly absorbing solutions, programming techniques used to facilitate data acquisition and investigations in the field of new coherent THz sources. The implementation and development of quasi-optic THz components is also described here. One of the group's aims is to establish metrological measures allowing comparison of results obtained using THz-TDS by various groups worldwide.

articleTitle: Numerical methods of structure-statistical object classification for remote sensing
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The main stage of solution of the structure-statistical object classification problem for remote sensing is the construction of probability distribution law on the base of probability learning sample. The structure of the solution of the problem includes the following five problems: the algorithm of construction of initial approximation of iterative process of estimation of mixed model parameters; the iterative process of EM-algorithm for estimation of distribution law parameters; criterion of the end of iterative EM-algorithm process; the determination of the number of components of mixed model of object feature-characteristic law distribution; statistical classification of objects of probability learning sample (PLS). The solution of each problem requires the building of new mathematical models, the creation of a number of simulation examples and computer programs, the improvement of existent algorithms for minimization of calculation time, and the check of program software on real computer data.

articleTitle: The approaches for increasing accuracy of N-fold differentiation of signals presented as Kotelnikov finite series
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The factors influencing the error of differentiation of signals with restricted domain of definition at usage of the mathematical apparatus based on Kotelnikov expansion are analyzed. The procedures permitting to increase the efficiency of differentiation are instanced.

articleTitle: On plasma antennas (State-of-the-art, actual problems, some results)
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The state-of-the-art and actual problems of plasma antennas (PA) are considered. An approach to approximate evaluation of the conductivity of two-component plasma is proposed. The loop PA impedance and efficiency at the UHF range are investigated. The results of computation for PA are compared with experimental data and the same results for the loop metal oscillator.

articleTitle: Development of the planar low-voltage cyclotron resonance maser with a sheet helical electron beam
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The design of a planar low-voltage cyclotron resonance maser (CRM) with the con-focal cavity, its geometry and results of the trajectory analysis for the planar magnetron - injection gun (MIG) are presented. Simulation results of dispersive characteristic of the confocal cavity and the distribution of an electromagnetic field for various cavity modes are described. The low-voltage CRM is designed for the frequency of 8 GHz with the water cooling magnetic system. Results of a computer simulation of wave particle interaction in the low-voltage CRM are also given.

articleTitle: Transition from the parabolic problem to the flat one and phantom
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Reduction of three-dimensional conical problem to two-dimensional (cylindrical, flat) has played a big role in the development of electromagnetic theory and its use in antenna technology. A similar result can be obtained by reducing the parabolic problem to the flat one. In this paper the relations between the coordinates of the two systems are derived, and a condition allowing the transition is described. The results are applied to the solving problem of the phantom shape and dimensions influence on the measurement results of the electric field generated by an external source outside of the phantom shell.

articleTitle: Plane circular array with steering time delay of pulse excitation
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Plane circular antenna as array of Tapered Slot Antennas (TSA) with video-pulse signals excitation has been proposed. The characteristics of space-time domain form of the field, radiated by plane circular array have been calculated and analyzed. Experimental measurement was done, which results were matched with the results of simulation. The possibility of radiation pattern synthesis through steaming time delay and excitation polarities at the elements of the circular array was proved.

articleTitle: Motion sensors based on dual-frequency integrated antennas-oscillators
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: This paper presents the results of research designed an integrated dual-frequency antennas-oscillators based on strip antennas as motion sensors. It is shown that the uses of dual-frequency mode allows reducing the absolute level of the amplitude of the information signal when a moving object is moved directly from the sensor antenna and reduce the impact of fluctuations of the generated oscillations amplitude on this signal simultaneously. In the first case it allows to minimize the impact of small moving objects, and the second - to increase the range of the sensor.

articleTitle: Managing of microwave antennas of digital combined radio relay-troposcatter station
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The usage of the communication systems in emergency situations is requiring the mobile stations of telecommunication. Therefore, the use of digital combined radio relay-troposcatter stations (DCRRTS) is fully justified. Proper selection of microwave antennas systems (MAS) largely determines the functional efficiency of mobile stations of telecommunication. In the elaboration of the DCRRTS one of the important issues is the selection of MAS that support two modes of operation: direct radio line (radio relay communication) and the out skyline (troposcatter communication). On the basis of the main advantages of reflector antennas - sufficient simplicity and reliability of a design, its transportability, the possibility of forming the required pattern, high gain, low noise temperature. This is the type of antennas is proposed to use in DCRRTS. For DCRRTS may be offered the next option to usage the following antennas: axisymmetric monoreflectible antenna for radio relay component of station and unaxisymmetric monoreflectible antenna for troposcatter component of station. Therefore there is a need to develop a control algorithm that automatically transfers station from one mode to another. This algorithm includes control of mechanical parts DCRRTS and its electrical characteristics.

articleTitle: Method of synthesis directional patterns of phased antenna array with arbitrary shape contour aperture
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Phased array antennas with an arbitrary contour aperture are now becoming more widely used in electronic systems for various purposes. This form of the aperture, in many cases determined by the terms of placement of radiators and/or combining them in a subarrays in order to reduce the number of control channels. In addition, the directional patterns of these antennas may have special requirements which determine, for example, a low level of side lobes and/or special law to the changes in the various directions. A distinctive feature of the amplitude-phase distribution in any planar aperture is its 2π-periodicity. In addition, this is true of the azimuthal dependence of the formed pattern and patterns of radiators. Accounting for this property and the associated orthogonality the Fourier series can develop a method allowing efficient calculations for solving the amplitude-phase synthesis on a given pattern. The article presents the mathematical basis of the method, we describe the results of numerical studies.

Author Keywords: plane aperture with an arbitrary contour
the method of synthesis of the radiation pattern

articleTitle: The method of synthesis of antenna with active elements
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The project presents an approach that solves present science problems of improvement of the radio systems with passive antennas via the active antennas application, which implements specification of the antennas of the radio systems during their design, development and application, increasing efficiency of their operation.

articleTitle: Estimation of broadband signal radiated by a single source in the presence of multiple acoustic interference sources via microphone array
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The scenario is considered when a mix of signals from multiple acoustic sources is received by a microphone array; the problem is to estimate the waveform of one of these sources. It is supposed that the position of the desired source is a priori known. The considered problem can arise in many applications like video conferencing, acoustic room surveillance and others, where it is necessary to capture human speech against acoustic interferences. To solve this problem, an adaptive algorithm is independently applied to each narrow band of the received signal. The adaptive algorithm employs the interference model consisting of a set of unknown steering vectors. It is known that most adaptive beamforming algorithms suffer from degradation due to imperfections in desired signal spatial model and finite sample size effect. The proposed method is shown to be quite robust to these effects. Such robustness is achieved without extra information about the error in the desired signal spatial model. The results of numerical modeling and experiments confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Field symmetry, reflected in the design of antennas
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Antenna possesses geometric properties that characterize the quality of resonance, antenna has a main purpose: to increase the probability of the observed sharp resonance. Spherical, conical symmetry, cylindrical, coaxial symmetry, the symmetry of plane and the square are the main types of symmetry, which characterize the change in the field and can be used in various combinations for constructing a spatial structure of antennas. Thus, it turns out that in the constructions is enough use of separate fragments of symmetry.

articleTitle: X-band substrate integrated waveguide antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The article deal with linear waveguide-slot antenna based on rectangular waveguide integrated into the substrate printed circuit board (substrate integrated waveguide) and intended for use in a circular array with one-dimensional scanning. Antenna design is a multilayer printed circuit board of the microwave dielectrics in which the top and bottom metal layers play the role of wide wall of waveguide, and the narrow wall of waveguide is formed by a series of metalized pins.

articleTitle: Initial guess selection for optimization of the given field distribution on the aperture of a leaky wave antenna
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: An algorithm of a good initial guess selection for optimization of an antenna field distribution is proposed. The parameters controlling the field distribution are the depth of grooves and the width of lamellas of a reflection grating scattering a surface wave of a planar dielectric waveguide. The algorithm uses the energy characteristic of a single groove. An example of optimization of the cosine on-a-pedestal field distribution is given.

articleTitle: On functional diversity of localised intervalley charge carrier transfer
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Possibilities of dramatic improvement in functionality by effects of bulk N-type Negative Differential Conductivity (N-NDC) in long inhomogeneous samples are described together with outstanding parameters of devices utilizing the effect.

articleTitle: The electrodinamical characteristics of two-way short-circuit slot in microstrip disk resonator
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The mathematical simulation for the structure which includes circular microstrip patch and radial two-way short-circuit slot realized with the help of finite element method. The spectral characteristics and current distribution on disk and energy characteristic were investigated. The sizes of structure were optimized and the possibility of matching such radiating structure in frequency domains was shown. Carried out experiments confirms, that microstrip disk antenna with single radial two-way short-circuit slot discontinuity have advantages like low level of VSWR, possibility of controlling of radiating power.

articleTitle: Multifrequency diagnostics of inhomogeneous media
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Method of electromagnetic scanning tomography and holography of subsurface objects based on the solution of inverse scattering problem for the pseudopulse synthesized by multifrequency measurements of the scattered field is studied. Results of its applications to diagnostics of various subsurface inhomogeneities are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Calculation and analysis of near field of dipole with corner reflector
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Algorithms and programs for calculating the characteristics of electric and magnetic fields (EMF) in the whole observation space in a near-field zone of the half-wave dipole with the corner reflector of infinite sizes and the aperture angle β=π/N (N is integer) have been developed. The amplitudes, phases and phase velocities of the transverse EMF components, also modulus and argument of their ratio in the normal direction to an aperture of the corner with different angles β were calculated versus the distance to observation point R/λ. It is shown that in a near-field zone the amplitude of H'φ- component decreases at increasing R/λ faster, than H'<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">θ</sub>, and that faster, than the corner aperture is less. The amplitude spatial distributions of the transverse EMF components of the dipole with plane screen are identical beginning with R= λ.

articleTitle: Electrodynamic analysis of disk nanoarrays
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Boundary problem of diffraction electromagnetic waves on two-dimensional periodic metal gratings have been solved with taking into account finite permittivity of metal in optic range. Suggested technique is based on approach of approximate boundary conditions for thin dielectric layers. It is pointed out that dependence of magnitude of scattered field on wavelength has resonant behavior and resonant wavelength is many times higher than size of cell of grating. It is shown the possibility of designing of grating with high reflection coefficient at frequencies of plasmon resonance.

articleTitle: A novel lens-integrated direct detection linear antenna array with narrow-gap hot-carrier bolometers for mm-wave imaging
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Experimental data on a narrowband bi-linear 16-element Schottky barrier diode detector antenna array for active mm-wave imaging systems and theoretical/experimental results on a novel ultrawideband linear 3-element hot-carrier bolometer lens-coupled antenna array for passive mm-wave imaging systems are presented.

articleTitle: Frame loop with switchable polarization
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Frame loop with controlled (switchable polarization) is described in the form of combination of four frames with perimeter length approximately equal to the wave length. By means of choosing the terminal points of feedline field radiation of linear vertical, horizontal and oblique polarizations is provided. The results of the numerical simulation are given herein.

articleTitle: Small VHF band antenna
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The results of the theoretical and experimental research of the small size wire system with logarithmic frequency. In this article construction principles of the band antennas based on logarithmic frequency which includes method of electrodynamics similarity and method of construction traveling-wave antenna. For traveling antenna at a fixed frequency three vibrators take part in the radiation: resonating vibrator, reflector and director. Resonating vibrator move to the top of traveling-wave antenna while frequency is increasing wherein maximum of radiation is directed along forming system of vibrators.

articleTitle: Parametric effects in not directed antennas, installed on the helicopter fuselage
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The paper shows that the system "A Standard Omnidirectional Antenna - Metal Body of the Helicopter" becomes non-parametric system at rotation of main rotor. Under this condition the effective height of the antenna is the parametric factor. Distortions of the spectrum of radio signals on the input of the standard antenna are consequence of periodic changes of the effective antenna height. In the paper, the method of analysis of signal spectrum after parametrical distortions is developed, namely: quantitative estimation of attenuation of spectral components of useful signal and detection of combination frequencies of unwanted components-satellites. Spectral distortions of some types of modulated and manipulated signals on the output of parametrical antenna system are also considered.

articleTitle: Method for the approximate simulation of complex large-scale structures
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The approach and computer program based on this approach for the approximate simulation of the microwave field distribution in the complex large-scale axial structures by using the theory of geometrical optics and the wave optics are described. The main idea of the method consists in the using of the beams tracing strategy. The comparison of results with known electrodynamic systems Ansoft HFSS and CST MWS are performed. It is shown that the adoption of this method provides sufficient accuracy in the calculation of the distribution of the bulk density of electromagnetic power in the treated material.

articleTitle: Signal estimation in the presence of the steering vector uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The problem of signal wave form estimation using an antenna array in case of uncertainties about the steering vector is considered. New asymptotically (in sample size) optimum estimators are derived. In contrast to the known optimal solutions, the employed method of synthesis yields non-iterative direct-form estimators. Simulation results are provided to evaluate the performance of the synthesized estimators.

articleTitle: Performance indicators of work quality of transport telecommunication primary network in Donetsk, Lviv and Odessa regions of Ukraine
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: In this work we present statistics data about number, nature and cause of underground fiber-optic communications lines damage, implemented on non-armored and armored cables of transport telecommunications primary network, for example, Donetsk, Lviv and Odessa regions in terms from 2001 to 2010 years.

articleTitle: The influence of antenna characteristics on information redundancy of communication channel
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The characteristics of atmosphere and antenna have a significant influence on information channels with information redundancy. Thus the research material concerning dependence identification of information redundancy from atmosphere and antenna parameters are represented in this report.

articleTitle: Works department of applied electrodynamics V. N. Karazin Kharkov National University in the field theory of near area antennas
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Department of Applied Electrodynamics the study of the theory of near-field antenna in 1970, the calculation of the characteristics of the fields in the near field of rectangular apertures. The result shows that, in the spotlight, beam incidence, the oscillation amplitudes of the fields are uneven and there is a region of space in which the amplitude of the field is close to a constant. Further investigated the polarization characteristics of aperture antennas with circular and elliptical polarization in the near field to clarify the criterion of the far field in the case of measuring the polarization characteristics of the antennas. Further research devoted wire antenna theory in the near zone. In particular, it is shown that the distance of the far zone of short wire antennas is R ≥ 0,6 wavelengths. It is also shown that in the case of resonance (half-wave new) wire antenna, the amplitude of the near-field hardly changed by the. Specified distance of the far zone aperture radiators that are smaller than the wavelength. Studied the wave processes in the near field of a traveling wave antenna. The possibility of creating an aperture antenna with a uniform distribution of the field amplitude in the plane or in the predetermined volume.

articleTitle: Phase optimization problems in antenna synthesis theory
publicationTitle: 2013 IX Internatioal Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: A short overview of the results obtained by the authors and their colleagues for a long time in the field of the antenna synthesis theory and the related problems of the field transformation is presented. The main common subject in all problems are the free phase functions ascribed to the given amplitude patterns of the antennas, or appearing as the phase corrections in the quasi-optical field transformers. The systems of specific types such as wave beam transformers and antennas with semitransparent surfaces, in particular, resonant and leaky-wave antennas are described. It is shown that some nonlinear integral equations arisen in the antenna synthesis problems with free phase (and their generalizations) have analytical solutions.
